summary: Living occurrences (GBIF), fossil occurrences (PBDB), a species-level synthetic tree (Open Tree) and sequence archives are all open, and two Dryad deposits map phylogenetic turnover across regions for single clades (Muroidea, butterflies); no resource joins living and fossil regional assemblages to an independent molecular tree with environmental covariates.
next_step: Restrict to one clade with a molecular tree and fossil record (e.g. a mammal order), build regional species lists from GBIF and PBDB, and pre-register the partitioning of turnover into ancestry and environment.
obstacles_confirmed: A tree built from the same traits that display the affinity would make the inheritance test circular.
Fossil and living taxonomies are unevenly linked.
Joint phylogenetic and geographic coverage is partial for the full living and fossil scope.
